articles.title: Heartbeats Raises $15 Million To Expand Digital Collectibles Platform
articles.snippet:
Heartbeats raised $15 million to expand ORICAL, its official digital collecting platform for sports and entertainment fans in Japan. Vertex Ventures Japan participated in the financing.
The post Heartbeats Raises $15 Million To Expand Digital Collectibles Platform appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Heartbeats Raises $15 Million To Expand Digital Collectibles Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Heartbeats Raises $15 Million To Expand Digital Collectibles Platform
Heartbeats raised $15 million to expand ORICAL, its official digital collecting platform for sports and entertainment fans in Japan. Vertex Ventures Japan participated in the financing.
Heartbeats operates ORICAL, a platform that allows fans to collect official digital trading cards featuring athletes, performers, and characters they support.
The platform currently spans categories including baseball, sumo, professional wrestling, and entertainment.
Heartbeats works directly with rights holders to create official collections and has partnerships with more than 20 content organizations.
Partners include the Chiba Lotte Marines, Hanshin Tigers, New Japan Pro-Wrestling, Hello! Project, the Takarazuka Revue, the Japan Sumo Association, and Tsuburaya Productions, the creator of Ultraman.
Heartbeats was founded in 2017 under the name ventus and rebranded as Heartbeats in January 2026.
The Tokyo-based company now employs 177 people.
Heartbeats developed ORICAL around the idea that sports and entertainment fans want more personalized ways to express which teams, athletes, performers, and characters they support.
The platform includes features supporting both online and real-world fan engagement.
Vertex Ventures Japan sees Heartbeats as part of a broader opportunity to support Japanese startups built around the country’s strengths in entertainment content and deep technology.
Vertex Ventures Japan was established in 2024 and operates as part of the global Vertex network supported by Vertex Holdings.
Its inaugural ¥10 billion fund, approximately $64 million, has invested in eight companies to date.
The firm plans to support portfolio companies such as Heartbeats by helping them access overseas customers and international business relationships through the broader Vertex network.
KEY QUOTES:
“We will strive to understand our fans more deeply than anyone else.”
Yuta Umesawa, Representative Director and CEO of Heartbeats
“What’s missing is global access.”
Takashi Tomita, Managing Partner at Vertex Ventures Japan

articles.title: Meticulous Raises $15 Million Series A Led By Chemistry To Expand Software Testing Platform
articles.snippet:
Meticulous raised $15 million in Series A funding to expand its software testing platform as AI coding tools accelerate the pace at which developers generate code. The round was led by Chemistry, with additional participation from Menlo Ventures.
The post Meticulous Raises $15 Million Series A Led By Chemistry To Expand Software Testing Platform appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Meticulous Raises $15 Million Series A Led By Chemistry To Expand Software Testing Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 9, 2026
Meticulous Raises $15 Million Series A Led By Chemistry To Expand Software Testing Platform
Meticulous raised $15 million in Series A funding to expand its software testing platform as AI coding tools accelerate the pace at which developers generate code. The round was led by Chemistry, with additional participation from Menlo Ventures.
Angel investors included former Stripe executive Lachy Groom; Poolside co-founder and co-CEO Jason Warner; Dropbox co-founder Arash Ferdowsi; former Adobe Chief Product Officer Scott Belsky; Vercel founder Guillermo Rauch; Segment founder and former OpenAI engineering lead Calvin French-Owen; Hex CTO Caitlin Colgrove; and former Cursor Head of Engineering Jason Ginsberg, who is now a Member of Technical Staff at xAI.
Meticulous is developing technology intended to address a growing bottleneck in AI-assisted software development: while AI agents can generate code increasingly quickly, testing and reviewing those changes can slow deployment.
The company provides an autonomous testing system that automatically creates and maintains thousands of user flows designed to cover edge cases across large software codebases.
Meticulous uses deterministic browsers and automated test generation, execution, and maintenance to reduce noise while identifying how software changes affect applications.
The platform can detect changes as small as a single-pixel difference across recorded user flows before code is shipped to production.
Its technology also gives engineers, product managers, and designers visibility into how proposed changes affect software before those changes are merged.
AI coding agents can use the same information to iterate on their own work before submitting it for human review.
Customers include Notion, ElevenLabs, Dropbox, Wiz, and LaunchDarkly.
KEY QUOTES:
“We’re moving into an era where code generation is relatively inexpensive, but that means code review and the feedback loop become the bottleneck. Meticulous helps us simultaneously move fast and raise the quality bar.”
Zach Davis, Director of Engineering at LaunchDarkly
“We piloted the tool, were immediately impressed and rolled it out across the entire engineering organization. Meticulous is unlike anything else, developers love it and it is now an essential guardrail of our software development process.”
Erdem Alparslan, Head of Developer Experience at Notion
“As we move closer and closer to truly exhaustive testing we’ve observed that this allows our customers to move at unprecedented speed. We’re excited to take the platform to the next level to allow another step change in velocity for our customers.”
Quentin Spencer-Harper, CTO of Meticulous
“Meticulous has built one of the most deeply loved products that I have come across in my eighteen years of investing.”
Ethan Kurzweil, Managing Partner at Chemistry

articles.title: Consano Bio Raises More Than $15 Million To Advance C-1101 For Chronic Sciatica
articles.snippet:
Consano Bio has raised more than $15 million in an oversubscribed financing to advance C-1101, its investigational multi-protein biologic therapy for chronic painful lumbosacral radiculopathy, also known as chronic sciatica.
The post Consano Bio Raises More Than $15 Million To Advance C-1101 For Chronic Sciatica appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Consano Bio Raises More Than $15 Million To Advance C-1101 For Chronic Sciatica
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 5, 2026
Consano Bio Raises More Than $15 Million To Advance C-1101 For Chronic Sciatica
Consano Bio has raised more than $15 million in an oversubscribed financing to advance C-1101, its investigational multi-protein biologic therapy for chronic painful lumbosacral radiculopathy, also known as chronic sciatica.
The financing exceeded the company’s $15 million target and was backed by a syndicate of accredited private investors.
Including the latest transaction, Consano Bio has raised more than $45 million since its founding three years ago.
The company plans to use the proceeds to complete its ongoing randomized, double-blind Phase 1 clinical trial of C-1101 and advance additional scientific and intellectual property work around C-1101 and other assets.
The C-1101-101 study is enrolling patients with chronic painful lumbosacral radiculopathy in Australia and the U.S.
Consano expects enrollment to be completed in early 2027, with clinical data anticipated during the first half of 2027.
Those results are intended to inform the next stages of clinical development.
The FDA granted C-1101 Fast Track designation for treatment of lumbosacral radiculopathy in August 2026.
Consano said there are currently no FDA-approved pharmaceutical treatments specifically for chronic sciatica.
C-1101 is a platelet-derived multi-protein biologic designed to modulate inflammation while stimulating and enhancing cellular repair at the site of injury.
The therapy contains consistent concentrations of cytokines, growth factors and matrix proteins and is delivered through an epidural injection directly to the site of nerve injury.
Consano is positioning C-1101 as a potential disease-modifying approach rather than a treatment focused solely on temporary symptom relief.
KEY QUOTE:
“C-1101 represents a new category of disease-modifying biologics, designed to activate cellular repair and alleviate the pain and dysfunction that results from orthopedic conditions. LSR is where we begin, and we believe the potential of this approach extends well beyond a single condition. The recently closed financing allows us to complete our first clinical study and to assess how C-1101 affects patients with chronic LSR versus an epidural saline injection. This is an exciting time for Consano Bio, and we are building toward what could transform how these conditions are treated.”
Andrew Hall, Chief Executive Officer of Consano Bio

articles.title: Medincell Secures €13.8 Million In Non-Dilutive Financing
articles.snippet:
Medincell has secured an additional €13.8 million in non-dilutive financing from European commercial banks and Bpifrance, bringing the biopharmaceutical company’s total non-dilutive financing secured since July 2026 to €41.8 million.
The post Medincell Secures €13.8 Million In Non-Dilutive Financing appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Medincell Secures €13.8 Million In Non-Dilutive Financing
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
Medincell Secures €13.8 Million In Non-Dilutive Financing
Medincell has secured an additional €13.8 million in non-dilutive financing from European commercial banks and Bpifrance, bringing the biopharmaceutical company’s total non-dilutive financing secured since July 2026 to €41.8 million.
The latest financing follows €28 million in non-dilutive bank financing announced in July. Medincell said the new capital was secured on market terms and does not include equity-linked instruments, meaning the financing will not dilute existing shareholders.
The company has also taken steps to reduce and extend its outstanding debt. In July 2026, Medincell repaid €23.2 million to the European Investment Bank, including €20 million of principal and related capitalized interest. The principal repayment represented 50% of its existing EIB financing facility.
Combined with the new financing, those actions have extended Medincell’s debt maturity profile through September 2031. The company reported €84.8 million in cash and cash equivalents as of March 31, 2026.
Medincell is a clinical- and commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company developing long-acting injectable medicines using its proprietary BEPO and BEPO Star drug-delivery technologies. The technologies are designed to enable controlled delivery of therapeutic drugs for periods ranging from several days to several months following a subcutaneous or local injection.
Risperidone LAI became the first treatment based on BEPO technology to receive FDA approval, initially for schizophrenia in April 2023 and subsequently for Bipolar I Disorder in October 2025. Teva markets the treatment in the U.S. under the UZEDY brand.
Medincell reached another commercial milestone in October 2026 when a once-monthly olanzapine long-acting injectable treatment for adults with schizophrenia received FDA approval. Teva plans to launch the product in the U.S. under the WELTRUZA brand during the fourth quarter of 2026. A European Marketing Authorization Application for the treatment was accepted by the European Medicines Agency in May 2026.
Beyond its commercial products, Medincell maintains a pipeline of therapeutic candidates ranging from formulation-stage programs through Phase 3 clinical trials. The Montpellier, France-based company employs more than 150 people representing over 27 nationalities and works with pharmaceutical companies and foundations to develop long-acting treatment options across multiple therapeutic areas.

articles.title: AI glasses brand NIMO secures angel funding at RMB 1.5 billion valuation
articles.snippet: AI glasses brand NIMO secures angel funding at RMB 1.5 billion valuation TechNode
articles.text:
The Chinese startup behind AI glasses brand NIMO has raised several hundred million yuan in angel funding, bringing its valuation to RMB 1.5 billion, according to an October 8 report. Investors include Gobi Partners, alongside other Chinese venture capital firms.
The company develops smart glasses for everyday use and has established offline sales channels. It plans to use the proceeds to develop new products and core technologies, expand its domestic retail network and enter overseas markets, as more Chinese hardware startups compete in AI eyewear. [ The Capital , in Chinese]
